questions.question: John Green's non-fiction book, released in March 2025, discusses the history and impact of which disease?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Tuberculosis**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Tuberculosis (TB)** is a highly contagious infectious disease caused by the bacterium **Mycobacterium tuberculosis**.
 
• The disease primarily affects the **lungs**, but it can also impact other parts of the body, such as the **spine, kidneys, and brain**.
 
• TB is one of the oldest known diseases in human history and continues to be a major cause of illness and death worldwide.
 
• It is typically spread through **airborne particles** when an infected person coughs, sneezes, or speaks.
 
• Symptoms of TB include **persistent cough, fever, night sweats, weight loss, and fatigue**.
 
• TB can be treated and cured with a combination of **antibiotics**, usually taken over a course of six months or longer.
 
• Efforts to combat TB include public health initiatives such as vaccination with the **BCG vaccine** and widespread screening programs.
 
• In 2025, John Green’s book likely explores the **historical impact** of TB, including its role in shaping public health systems and its representation in literature and culture.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Influenza**__

 __
 
• **Influenza**, commonly known as the flu, is caused by the **influenza virus**.
 
• It primarily affects the **respiratory system** and spreads through **airborne droplets** or contact with contaminated surfaces.
 
• Influenza pandemics, such as the **Spanish Flu of 1918**, have caused widespread fatalities.
 
• Vaccination is the primary method of prevention, and antiviral medications are used for treatment.
 
 
 
• **Malaria**__
 __
 
• **Malaria** is caused by parasites of the genus **Plasmodium**, transmitted through the bites of infected **Anopheles mosquitoes**.
 
• It is prevalent in tropical and subtropical regions, especially in **Sub-Saharan Africa**.
 
• Symptoms include **fever, chills, headache, and vomiting**.
 
• Malaria can be prevented with the use of **mosquito nets, insect repellents, and antimalarial drugs.**
 
 
 
• **Cholera**__
 
 
• **Cholera** is an acute diarrheal disease caused by the bacterium **Vibrio cholerae**.
 
• It is commonly transmitted through **contaminated water or food**.
 
• Symptoms include severe **dehydration, watery diarrhea, and vomiting**.
 
• Improving access to clean water and sanitation is critical for preventing cholera outbreaks.

questions.solution:

questions.question: What amount will be disbursed from FY 2020-21 to FY 2025-26 under the Agriculture Infrastructure Fund established by the Central Government?

questions.question:
Which of the following statements related to the One Nation One Subscription (ONOS) scheme launched in 2024 is/are correct?

Statement 1: The ONOS scheme aims to provide digital access to over 13,000 international journals for research institutions across India.

Statement 2: INFLIBNET(Information and Library Network) is responsible for managing financial transactions related to the subscription charges of these journals.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is option 3,

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The One Nation One Subscription (ONOS) scheme was launched in 2024 to provide **universal digital access to academic resources** for research institutions and universities across India.
 
• Under ONOS, over **13,000 international journals and publications** are made accessible to researchers, students, and faculties free of cost.
 
• The scheme aims to reduce the financial burden on individual institutions by allowing centralized government negotiation for subscriptions.
 
• The focus of ONOS is to ensure **equitable access to global academic resources** across both rural and urban institutions, fostering growth in research and development.
 
• Statement 2 is incorrect as **INFLIBNET is not responsible for financial transactions**. Instead, it provides technical support for platform integration and resource access.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **INFLIBNET (Information and Library Network Centre):**

 
 
• It is an autonomous Inter-University Centre under the University Grants Commission (UGC).
 
• INFLIBNET facilitates access to scholarly content and supports the integration of library networks in India.
 
• It developed platforms like **Shodhganga** and **e-ShodhSindhu** to promote open access and research collaboration.
 
 
 
• **Centralized Subscription Model:**
 
 
• This model ensures that the government negotiates subscriptions for academic resources on behalf of all institutions.
 
• It eliminates redundancy and reduces costs for individual institutions.
 
 
 
• **Impact on Research Ecosystem:**
 
 
• ONOS is expected to boost India's research output by providing seamless access to global resources.
 
• It aims to bridge the gap between institutions in rural and urban areas.
 
 
 
• **Global Academic Resources:**
 
 
• These include journals, databases, and conference proceedings that are crucial for academic research.
 
• The ONOS initiative ensures access to resources from leading publishers and organizations worldwide.

questions.question: In March 2025, India introduced anti-dumping duties on five products imported from which country?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is option 1,

The correct answer is __**China**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Anti-dumping duties are imposed to protect domestic industries from unfair trade practices such as the dumping of cheap foreign goods at below-market prices.
 
• India introduced anti-dumping duties on five products originating from China in March 2025, aiming to prevent harm to local manufacturers.
 
• The targeted products included chemicals, steel products, and consumer goods, which were found to be sold below fair market value.
 
• This action was taken following investigations by the Directorate General of Trade Remedies (DGTR) under the Ministry of Commerce and Industry.
 
• The duties are compliant with WTO norms, ensuring fair trade while safeguarding India's economic interests.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Anti-Dumping Duty:**

 
 
• It is a protectionist tariff imposed by a government on imports that are priced below their normal value in the exporting country.
 
• Aims to safeguard domestic industries from predatory pricing practices by foreign exporters.
 
• Dumping can lead to market distortions and long-term damage to domestic production capabilities.
 
 
 
• **World Trade Organization (WTO) Guidelines:**
 
 
• Anti-dumping measures must comply with WTO’s Anti-Dumping Agreement.
 
• Governments must conduct investigations to prove dumping and its impact on domestic industries.
 
• WTO allows countries to impose duties only to the extent necessary to counteract harm caused by dumping.
 
 
 
• **Directorate General of Trade Remedies (DGTR):**
 
 
• It is India's apex authority for investigating unfair trade practices such as dumping and subsidies.
 
• DGTR operates under the Ministry of Commerce and Industry.
 
• It recommends anti-dumping duties and countervailing measures based on its investigations.
 
 
 
• **Impact of Anti-Dumping Duties:**
 
 
• Protects domestic industries from unfair competition.
 
• Encourages fair pricing and trade practices globally.
 
• May lead to increased prices for consumers but is aimed at ensuring long-term economic stability.

questions.question: The Dedicated Freight Corridor Corporation of India Limited (DFCCIL) was established as a Special Purpose Vehicle (SPV) under which of the following Acts?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Companies Act, 1956**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Dedicated Freight Corridor Corporation of India Limited (DFCCIL) was established in **October 2006** as a Special Purpose Vehicle (SPV).
 
• It was created under the **Companies Act, 1956**, to develop, mobilize resources, and operate dedicated freight corridors in India.
 
• DFCCIL operates under the administrative control of the **Ministry of Railways**, Government of India.
 
• The primary objective of DFCCIL is to **decongest India’s railway network** and improve freight transportation efficiency.
 
• It is responsible for planning and executing the construction of **Eastern and Western Dedicated Freight Corridors**, among other freight projects.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Dedicated Freight Corridor (DFC)**

 
 
• A Dedicated Freight Corridor is a high-capacity rail network exclusively for freight transportation.
 
• India’s Eastern DFC spans from Ludhiana in Punjab to Dankuni in West Bengal, while the Western DFC runs from Dadri in Uttar Pradesh to Jawaharlal Nehru Port in Maharashtra.
 
• These corridors aim to reduce logistics costs, promote economic growth, and enhance supply chain efficiency.
 
 
 
• **Companies Act, 1956**
 
 
• It was a comprehensive legislation governing the registration, regulation, and dissolution of companies in India.
 
• The Act focused on ensuring accountability, transparency, and fair practices in corporate governance.
 
• The Companies Act, 1956, has since been replaced by the **Companies Act, 2013**, but many organizations like DFCCIL were initially incorporated under the 1956 Act.
 
 
 
• **SPV (Special Purpose Vehicle)**
 
 
• An SPV is a legal entity created for a specific purpose, such as infrastructure development.
 
• It allows separate financial and operational management for distinct projects.
 
• DFCCIL was set up as an SPV to facilitate better management of freight corridor projects.
 
 
 
• **Ministry of Railways**
 
 
• The Ministry of Railways oversees India’s railway network, including freight corridors.
 
• It works towards modernizing rail infrastructure and enhancing operational efficiency.

questions.question: How many villages in India have completed the computerisation of land records as of March 2025, according to the Department of Land Resources?

__
 
• As of March 2025, the Department of Land Resources reported that **6.25 lakh villages** in India have completed the computerisation of land records.
 
• This initiative is part of the **Digital India Land Records Modernization Programme (DILRMP)**, which aims to enhance transparency and reduce disputes in land ownership.
 
• The computerisation process involves **digitising land records, integrating textual and spatial data, and ensuring easy access** to land-related information for citizens.
 
• The programme plays a pivotal role in **reducing corruption and ensuring efficient land management** by creating a unified digital database.
 
• India's progress in this domain contributes to achieving the **United Nations Sustainable Development Goal (SDG) 16**, which focuses on promoting peace, justice, and strong institutions.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Digital India Land Records Modernization Programme (DILRMP):**

 
 
• Launched in 2008, it was revamped under the **Digital India initiative** in 2016.
 
• Aims to computerise land records, enhance transparency, and reduce litigation over land disputes.
 
• The programme involves three key components: computerisation of land records, survey/resurvey of lands, and integration of land records with revenue courts.
 
 
 
• **Benefits of Computerised Land Records:**
 
 
• Improved transparency in land transactions and ownership.
 
• Reduced fraud and corruption in land dealings.
 
• Easy access to land records for citizens, enabling quicker grievance redressal.
 
 
 
• **Challenges in Land Records Modernisation:**
 
 
• Legacy issues with inaccurate and incomplete records.
 
• Lack of uniformity across states in land record maintenance systems.
 
• Limited digital literacy in rural areas to access digital records.
 
 
 
• **Global Practices:**
 
 
• Countries like Estonia and Sweden have implemented advanced land record systems with blockchain technology to ensure transparency and security.
 
• India's efforts under DILRMP aim to replicate such success stories with contextual modifications.

__
 
• **Yoko Ogawa** is a renowned Japanese author known for her literary works that explore memory, relationships, and human psychology.
 
• The novel "**Mina's Matchbox**" was originally written in **Japanese**, showcasing Ogawa's rich storytelling style and cultural depth.
 
• Yoko Ogawa has received numerous accolades for her works, including the prestigious **Akutagawa Prize**, which is one of Japan's top literary awards.
 
• The English translation of "**Mina's Matchbox**" was scheduled for release on **2 August 2024**, enabling her stories to reach a global audience.
 
• Ogawa's works have been translated into multiple languages, making her a celebrated author internationally.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Japanese Literature:**

 
 
• Japanese literature has a long and rich history, spanning classical, modern, and contemporary works.
 
• Notable authors include **Haruki Murakami**, **Yasunari Kawabata**, and **Kenzaburō Ōe**, with Kawabata and Ōe being Nobel Prize winners.
 
• Genres range from haiku poetry and historical narratives to modern novels exploring existential themes.
 
• Japanese literature emphasizes minimalism, nature, and deep emotional introspection.
 
 
 
• **Translation in Literature:**
 
 
• Translating literary works involves not just converting language but also preserving cultural nuances and emotional depth.
 
• Renowned translators like **Stephen Snyder** have worked on Ogawa's novels, ensuring their integrity in English.
 
• Translations play a crucial role in bridging cultural gaps and introducing regional authors to global audiences.
 
 
 
• **Yoko Ogawa's Notable Works:**
 
 
• **The Housekeeper and the Professor**: A heartwarming story about relationships and memory.
 
• **The Memory Police**: A dystopian novel exploring themes of erasure and loss.
 
• Ogawa's works often delve into human emotions and the subtle complexities of everyday life.
 
 
 
• **Global Reception of Japanese Literature:**
 
 
• Japanese authors have gained widespread recognition for their unique storytelling and cultural perspectives.
 
• Many novels have become international bestsellers, reflecting universal themes and resonating with diverse audiences.
 
• The popularity of Japanese literature has been bolstered by English translations and adaptations.
